title: Compact Endpoint Profiles: PRD and Gated Rollout Checklist
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
This PRD defines 'Compact Endpoint Profiles' — curated, opinionated endpoint configurations that group common inference surfaces (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank) into a small set of opt-in profiles for hosted customers. Each profile prescribes model variant, batching and caching defaults, latency SLO bands, and quality targets tailored to a specific cost/latency trade-off. The goal is to provide an easy on-ramp for teams to pick an endpoint profile that aligns with their org-level constraints, reducing time-to-production and operational load while preserving predictable economics.

Goals:
- Ship 3 compact profiles (Fast, Balanced, Economical) that cover 80% of expected customer workloads for first 90 days.
- Provide unified API surface so customers can switch profiles without code changes (profile selector in request).
- Reduce mean cost-per-token for 'Economical' profile by at least 30% compared to baseline hosted default.
- Achieve latency SLOs per profile: Fast p50 < 120ms, Balanced p50 < 220ms, Economical p50 < 400ms for typical prompt sizes (<= 512 tokens).

Non-goals:
- Not a full replacement for Dedicated or Private offerings.
- Not supporting multi-modal inputs in v1.

Scope and Surfaces:
- Endpoints: /v1/chat (chat-style), /v1/completions, /v1/embeddings, /v1/rerank. Each endpoint accepts an optional header or query param 'x-profile: fast|balanced|economical'.
- Default server-side routing to a profile when param omitted: falls back to 'Balanced'.
- Prescribed defaults per profile: model family, quantization level, batch window, KV cache policy, prefix caching TTL.
- Telemetry hooks: token-cost estimation, latency breakdown, model-fallback events surfaced to Console.

Clarifications / Decisions to Record:
- Model mapping: 'Fast' uses small low-latency variants (quantized if available); 'Balanced' uses higher-quality mid-size variants; 'Economical' uses aggressive quantization + batching + longer batch window. Decision: select model mapping from approved model catalog (research/ops to provide final mapping by 2026-03-05).
- Determinism: no deterministic guarantees for Economical profile due to caching/batching heuristics; doc will clearly mark behavior differences.
- Compatibility: embeddings must preserve vector dimensionality; rerank returns stable ordering per request but internal scoring thresholds may vary by profile.

Scope Changes (Recorded during scoping):
- 2026-02-24: Initial scope included only chat and completions. During PM/Eng sync, added embeddings and rerank to better surface tenant-level cost controls. This increases test matrix and required QA time by ~30%.
- 2026-02-28: Reduced availability of 'Economical' profile in APAC regions for v1 due to GPU capacity constraints; documented fallback policy to 'Balanced' in APAC.

Requirements (functional and non-functional):
- Functional:
  - F1: API accepts 'x-profile' and routes requests to matching serving configuration.
  - F2: Console shows per-profile cost/latency breakdown and allows org admins to set org-default profile.
  - F3: SDKs expose profile selector with typed enum and inlined docs.
  - F4: Model fallback: if a selected profile's model is unavailable, automatically fallback to a compatible variant in the same profile family and emit a 'fallback' metric.
- Non-functional:
  - N1: Per-profile latency SLOs as listed in Goals.
  - N2: 99.9% availability on hosted control plane for profile selection/routing.
  - N3: Monitoring must emit per-profile token cost and quality regression alerts.

Acceptance Criteria (must be met before 'In Review' -> 'Planned' -> 'Launch'):
- AC1: End-to-end API test harness verifies profile routing and returns expected model id header for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank for 10 sampled prompt sizes.
- AC2: Performance tests: each profile meets p50 and p95 latency targets under representative load (see perf matrix) across three regions (US-EAST, EU-WEST, APAC-limited).
- AC3: Cost regression: 'Economical' profile shows >=30% token-cost reduction in synthetic workloads vs baseline.
- AC4: Console: per-profile dashboard panel renders (cost, latency, fallback counts) and admin can set org default (e2e test included).
- AC5: SDKs: client bindings (Python/Node) include profile param and pass unit tests for serialization and header propagation.
- AC6: Security & Compliance: security review completed and no blocking findings; KMS usage for any customer-managed keys validated if used in Private variants.
- AC7: Rollout runbook and rollback plan documented and reviewed by SRE and Support.

Gated Rollout Checklist (pre-launch -> canary -> ramp -> GA):
- Pre-launch (all items required):
  - PRs merged for routing logic, model-mapping config, Console UI, SDK updates, and integration tests. (links: Confluence PRD, GitHub PRs TBD).
  - Perf harness completed and benchmark report attached.
  - Security review: completed.
  - Support runbook written and distributed.
  - Observability: dashboards, alerts, and per-profile metrics instrumented.
- Canary (2 weeks):
  - Phase 1: Enable 'Economical' for internal accounts and 2 pilot customers (opt-in). Monitor 1-min aggregated fallback rate, per-profile p95 latency, error rate, and cost-per-token.
  - Gate for ramp: fallback rate < 1%, p95 latency within 1.5x SLO, error rate delta < 0.05%.
- Ramp (3–4 weeks):
  - Gradual increase: 5% -> 25% -> 50% of new customers by profile opt-in. At each step, run synthetic workloads and check regressions.
  - APAC: keep 'Economical' restricted until capacity expansion; auto-fallback behavior must be validated.
- GA:
  - Final checklist: sign-offs from Eng, SRE, Product, Support, Security. Documentation published. SDKs released.

Monitoring & Rollback Triggers:
- Immediate rollback to prior routing config if any of the following sustained for >10 minutes:
  - global error rate increases by >0.5% absolute vs baseline,
  - per-profile p95 latency exceeds 3x SLO,
  - fallback rate > 5% for >15 minutes,
  - cost anomalies detected (cost per token > 2x expected for a profile).

Telemetry & QA items:
- Instrument 'profile' in request traces, model-id header, batching window used, and fallback reason.
- Add synthetic test suite to run nightly across prompt size matrix for all 4 endpoints.

Dependencies & Risks:
- Dependencies:
  - Model Ops: finalize model mapping by 2026-03-05.
  - Runtime team: kernel selection flags and quantization paths for selected models.
  - Console team: panel and org-default settings.
  - SDK owners: release coordinated minor version.
- Risks:
  - Risk: Economical profile might introduce higher failure modes due to aggressive quantization; Mitigation: extend canary, add quality regression checks.
  - Risk: Customers confused by behavior differences across profiles; Mitigation: explicit docs, in-console comparisons, default profile nudges.

notes: This ticket is intended as the canonical product contract for compact endpoint profiles. Implementation details (exact model ids, quantization knobs) will be recorded in runtime feature flags and separate ENG tickets.
postmortem_plan: If rollout causes customer impact, perform immediate rollback, collect traces for 1 hour, convene war room with Product/ENG/SRE/Support and publish a short incident report within 48 hours.
communication_plan: Customer-facing doc + blog post at GA, targeted emails to pilot customers during Canary, and in-console notification when org-default profile changes.
